name: Rajan Kolhapuri — Leather Craftsman
excerpt: The Kolhapuri chappal is a UNESCO-recognized craft — hand-stitched leather sandals from Maharashtra that have been worn since before colonial times. Rajan's workshop in Dharavi is one of the last to make them the old way.
body:
Kolhapuri chappals are named for the city of Kolhapur in Maharashtra, where the craft originated. The sandals are made from vegetable-tanned leather, hand-punched with elaborate geometric patterns, and stitched using a single thick thread.

Rajan Kolhapuri — a surname he chose when he moved to Mumbai twenty years ago — works in a narrow shop in Dharavi. He makes forty pairs a month. The genuine article takes three days per pair.

The problem is simple: machine-made chappals from factories in Agra look identical to a casual buyer and cost one-tenth as much.

"My grandfather made chappals for the district collector, the maharaja's household," Rajan says. "My father made them for families who had worn Kolhapuri for three generations. I make them for people who know the difference. That market is not growing."

He is training his daughter. She is not certain she will continue. "I tell her: learn it first. Decide later. You cannot unlearn a craft."
